title: Allied Trades Warrant Officer.
raw_text:
8-914A. Military Occupational Specialty 914A--Allied Trades Warrant Officer. (Eff 202010)
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. AR 135-100, DA Pam 601-6, and DA Pam 611-21.
    c. MOS 914A. MOS 914A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are 91E or
91X/91Z with 91E experience.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASIs associated with all
warrant officer MOS)).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Complete the Allied Trades Warrant Officer Basic Course.
               (b) Have correctable vision, normal color discrimination, normal hearing, and full use
of upper and lower extremities per AR 40-501.                                   .
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Complete the Allied Trades Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
         (3) CW4 must—-
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
         (4) CW5 must—-see MOS 915E.
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Directs the setup, operation, and maintenance of machine tools, computer
numerical control (CNC), and welding equipment used to fabricate or repair parts, mechanisms,
tools, and machinery.
               (b) Manages automotive body, frame, and hull repair, painting, glass, radiator,
canvas, and woodworking shop operations.
               (c) Supervises and conducts recovery operations and maintenance of tracked and
wheeled recovery equipment.
               (d) Employs principles of mechanics, metals identification procedures, shop
mathematics, and shop layout.
               (e) Establishes and directs the upkeep of shop stock, materials, and maintenance-
related items required per applicable regulations.
               (f) Manages quality assurance and production control programs to ensure
established work standards are met and repairs are made on a timely basis.
               (g) Establishes training programs to ensure subordinates are qualified in current
maintenance techniques and equipment operation.
               (h) Coordinates shop activities with other repair shops to ensure equipment is quickly
repaired and returned to user.
               (i) Establishes and conducts a shop safety program per applicable regulations.
               (j) Administers The Army Maintenance Management System (TAMMS).
        (2) CW3--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
               (b) Manages personnel and activities in field level maintenance within Echelons
above Brigade organizations.
        (3) CW4—
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
               (b) Serves as the senior allied trades technical advisor in echelons above brigade levels
of command.
               (c) Assists echelons above brigade staff in the planning, coordination, and execution of
maintenance support.
               (d) Provides technical expertise in allied trades doctrine on the battlefield for brigade
and subordinate element level commanders and staff to efficiently employ allied trades personnel
and equipment in support of the commanders’ mission.
              (e) Manages materiel readiness reporting for echelons above brigade organizations.
              (f) Performs materiel readiness management duties at sustainment command levels.
              (g) Performs research, development, test and evaluation duties.
              (h) Assists in coordination and evaluates allied trades tasks performed by contract
support.
              (i) Serves as Ordnance technical subject matter expert in training, capability, and
materiel development positions.
              (j) Advises commanders on the progression and utilization of subordinate Ordnance
warrant officers.
         (4) CW5—-see MOS 915E.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A minimum OPAT score of (Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles)
in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-914A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-914A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

matches: Develop testing and evaluation procedures.
Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
Set up and operate machine tools to repair or fabricate machine parts, jigs, fixtures, or tools.
(a) Directs the setup, operation, and maintenance of machine tools, computer numerical control (CNC), and welding equipment used to fabricate or repair parts, mechanisms, tools, and machinery.
Perform routine repair and maintenance duties.
(b) Manages automotive body, frame, and hull repair, painting, glass, radiator, canvas, and woodworking shop operations.
Implement or perform preventive maintenance, backup, or recovery procedures.
(c) Supervises and conducts recovery operations and maintenance of tracked and wheeled recovery equipment.
Compute dimensions, tolerances, and angles of workpieces or machines according to specifications and knowledge of metal properties and shop mathematics.
(d) Employs principles of mechanics, metals identification procedures, shop mathematics, and shop layout.
Maintain inventory, ordering materials as required.
(e) Establishes and directs the upkeep of shop stock, materials, and maintenance- related items required per applicable regulations.
Establish production or quality control standards.
(f) Manages quality assurance and production control programs to ensure established work standards are met and repairs are made on a timely basis.
Conduct or arrange for worker training in safety, repair, or maintenance techniques, operational procedures, or equipment use.
(g) Establishes training programs to ensure subordinates are qualified in current maintenance techniques and equipment operation.
Arrange for repairs of equipment or machinery.
(h) Coordinates shop activities with other repair shops to ensure equipment is quickly repaired and returned to user.
Enforce safety rules and regulations.
(i) Establishes and conducts a shop safety program per applicable regulations.
Oversee the maintenance and repair of machinery, equipment, and electrical and mechanical systems.
(j) Administers The Army Maintenance Management System (TAMMS).
Assign and review the work of subordinates.
(a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
Perform facilities maintenance work, such as constructing or repairing structures or controlling weeds or pests.
(b) Manages personnel and activities in field level maintenance within Echelons above Brigade organizations.
Determine work assignments and procedures.
(3) CW4— (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
Oversee support staff.
(c) Assists echelons above brigade staff in the planning, coordination, and execution of maintenance support.
Provide technical expertise or support related to manufacturing.

(d) Provides technical expertise in allied trades doctrine on the battlefield for brigade and subordinate element level commanders and staff to efficiently employ allied trades personnel and equipment in support of the commanders’ mission.
Compile and prepare reports and documents pertaining to personnel activities.
(e) Manages materiel readiness reporting for echelons above brigade organizations.
Maintain or repair agricultural facilities, equipment, or tools to ensure operational readiness, safety, and cleanliness.
(f) Performs materiel readiness management duties at sustainment command levels.
Develop testing and evaluation procedures.
(g) Performs research, development, test and evaluation duties.
Direct and coordinate the activities of staff and contract personnel and evaluate their performance.
(h) Assists in coordination and evaluates allied trades tasks performed by contract support.
Provide technical expertise or support related to manufacturing.
(i) Serves as Ordnance technical subject matter expert in training, capability, and materiel development positions.
Supervise or advise subordinate personnel.
(j) Advises commanders on the progression and utilization of subordinate Ordnance warrant officers.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
